statuses.PROVEN: Behavior has evidence and may be implemented.
statuses.UNPROVEN: Do not guess. Stop, count or use an explicitly reported engine policy.
statuses.CONTRADICTED: A hypothesis conflicts with measured behavior; implementation must follow the evidence.
statuses.APPROXIMATED: Garden deliberately implements incomplete engine behavior and reports every reliance.
statuses.ENGINE_POLICY: A deliberate Garden decision about what the runtime does or refuses, not a claim about the engine.

source_categories.public_documentation: Fallout 4 Creation Kit wiki, its offline mirror, or another public Papyrus document.
source_categories.project_authored_black_box_probe: A project-authored script, fixture or probe run through a locally installed Bethesda tool as a black box.
source_categories.local_corpus_measurement: A measurement over a lawfully obtained local shipped or mod corpus. Counts only are published.
source_categories.read_only_community_declarations: Read-only declarations from a community tool such as xEdit or Mutagen, used as a reference, never as implementation text.
source_categories.private_reverse_engineering_research: Private research on a local installation. Only sanitized factual conclusions reach this registry.
source_categories.project_build_measurement: A fact recorded by building or testing this project's own code.

rows.source_detail: Garden token completion tests establish an internal contract only; no Fallout latent-native scheduling probe has run.
rows.factual_conclusion: Latent native waits remain gated. Garden can retain a token and frame until an explicit answer, but this does not establish Fallout timing, save persistence or engine scheduling semantics.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Fallout latent-native completion timing, detach handling and external-answer persistence are unproven. Probe a script waiting beyond eight scheduler steps, answer delivery once, detach/reattach and save/restore.
rows.provenance_boundary: Garden tests prove only the gated internal contract, not engine compatibility.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the dialogue fragment dispatcher.
rows.factual_conclusion: A topic-info line runs its begin and end fragments on the shared host with the arguments Radicle decoded, but only once the fragment timing is proven. A line whose conditions cannot be decided is blocked rather than played, and a line whose native support is unproven is blocked and named.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden dispatch contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: When a topic-info fragment fires relative to the line has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: While the timing is unproven nothing runs and the line is counted, so a fragment is never fired at a guessed moment.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: When the begin and end fragments of a topic-info fire relative to the line, and with which arguments.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as a named blocker rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: The dialogue natives are not implemented.
rows.factual_conclusion: The dialogue natives are a named blocker: a line that needs them is blocked and counted rather than played with unproven support.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Which dialogue natives the load order uses and what each one does.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as a named blocker rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the scene runtime.
rows.factual_conclusion: Start, stop and pause control Garden scene state; a second start while playing is refused. Stop resets the phase. Phase fragments and advancement require Playing as well as their own allowed evidence keys.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden state contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: When a scene phase ends and the next begins has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: Phase advancement is a named dependency: it is refused and counted, and the phase does not change, so the missing scene runtime behaviour is never guessed.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: When a scene phase ends and the next begins, and what drives that transition.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as a named dependency rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the story-manager paths.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every story node is decided by its own condition list first: an indeterminate list dispatches nothing and names the undecided functions, a decided-false list skips the node. A supported node then starts its quest through the caller's callback or delivers its event to the quest's owner through the C2 bridge, and an unimplemented family is counted and named.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden dispatch contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The story event families beyond quest start and script delivery are not implemented.
rows.factual_conclusion: An unimplemented story event family dispatches nothing and is counted, so an unsupported family is never dropped or fired as if it were supported.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's full story event family set and what each family does.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as counted rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the gameplay native adapters.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every gameplay native names the Garden system that owns it. A native whose system exists is bound as an adapter into that system and writes the same authoritative state the runtime reads; a native whose system does not exist stays unbound and is counted with the missing system named.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden adapter contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The actor-value, faction, AI, movement, combat and crime systems do not exist in Garden.
rows.factual_conclusion: Six gameplay native families have no owning Garden system, so their natives stay unbound and are counted with the missing system named rather than silently returning nothing.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What each of those families reads or changes in the engine, and which Garden system will own it.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as absent rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the UI service binding.
rows.factual_conclusion: UI bindings require a supplied service and an allowed binding key. Debug.Notification and Debug.MessageBox reach that service. Message.Show stops if the latent key is not allowed; allowed latent results retain a token. UI.OpenMenu stays unbound without a Garden implementation. Fragments require their own key.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden service contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The engine's own menu, message and terminal behaviour has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: What the engine shows for a menu or message, and when a terminal fragment fires, is not proven. Garden routes the calls into its own UI service and counts what it refuses.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's menu, message and terminal behaviour and the timing of terminal fragments.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than inferred from Garden's service.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the save state.
rows.factual_conclusion: A suspended thread is stored with the fingerprint of the script it was suspended against, so a restore resumes it at its own program counter only when the fingerprint matches; a changed script and an absent script are each rejected and counted rather than resumed at a guessed position. Owner keys round-trip unchanged, and the typed payloads survive the serialized form.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden save contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The engine's own save format and what it stores for a Papyrus thread has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: Garden's save state is its own format. Whether the engine stores the same state, and how it treats a changed script on load, is not proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's save format for Papyrus runtime state and its behaviour when a script changed between save and load.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than inferred from Garden's format.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the Part C closure gate.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every remaining unsupported or unverified row names only an open evidence key or a missing Garden system, and no Part C task may stay open. A row an implementation consumes may not stay unproven; a row with no consumer must be an unrun probe or a named missing system; a contradicted row is closed because the refutation is recorded. A clean result is not a compatibility claim.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden bookkeeping gate, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the compatibility gate.
rows.factual_conclusion: The gate is the only place that may permit a full runtime compatibility claim, and it permits one only when the closure gate is clean and no missing-system blocker remains. Open evidence keys may remain because they stop only the behaviour they describe. A refused claim names every missing system and every open key, and the recorded registry does not satisfy the claim.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden gate contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the archive script source.
rows.factual_conclusion: The cache asks an injected archive reader for one entry at a time and never parses a container itself, because Radicle decodes it. An entry the reader cannot produce is refused and counted rather than reported as an empty script, a loose script of the same name shadows the archived copy, and an unproven key reads nothing.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden adapter contract, not a claim about a real archive.

rows.source_detail: Byte-identity round trips over a local/private .pex corpus; PluginEditTool Papyrus engineering record.
rows.factual_conclusion: The container is little-endian with magic 0xFA57C0DE; Fallout 4 is game id 2 at format 3.9. The big-endian Skyrim magic and foreign game ids are rejected before any field is trusted.
rows.provenance_boundary: Field layout and rejection behavior only. No corpus file, name or content is committed or published.

rows.source_detail: Corpus round trips plus the project's own writer and the PluginEditTool Papyrus record.
rows.factual_conclusion: The instruction set has 47 opcodes including the Fallout 4 additions; callmethod, callparent and callstatic are the three variable-argument opcodes.
rows.provenance_boundary: Opcode numbers and operand shapes only. No proprietary implementation text.

rows.source_detail: 1,496 loose .pex measured; 1,480 count the size field's own four bytes, 16 count only the body.
rows.factual_conclusion: The per-object size field has two conventions in the wild. PexObject::sizeIncludesItself records which one a file used; the majority convention is the default.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The producing toolchain is not identified.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts and the two conventions only.

rows.source_detail: Corpus round trips; files exist whose last object is followed by further bytes.
rows.factual_conclusion: Some files carry bytes past the last object. PexFile::trailingBytes preserves them instead of dropping or interpreting them.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What produces those bytes is not identified.
rows.provenance_boundary: Presence and preservation only.

rows.source_detail: Corpus round trips; no measured file has a duplicate string.
rows.factual_conclusion: The string table is carried verbatim rather than rebuilt on read, and first-occurrence lookup is safe because no measured file has a duplicate entry.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts and the reuse rule only.

rows.source_detail: Synthetic fixture whose string table holds 0x80 0xA9 0xFE 0xFF, read through the C ABI and the managed model.
rows.factual_conclusion: Strings are length-prefixed with a u16 and stored one byte per character. The reader, the C ABI and the managed model return those bytes unchanged.
rows.provenance_boundary: Synthetic fixture only; no corpus content.

rows.source_detail: No public document and no probe settles the character encoding of bytes at or above 0x80.
rows.factual_conclusion: Latin-1 is the reading the C++ and C# layers apply to the stored bytes. Any other character encoding is unproven and is not implemented.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Which character encoding the engine uses for non-ASCII script strings.
rows.provenance_boundary: Byte preservation is proven; the encoding is not.

rows.source_detail: Garden's support boundary, not a claim about the engine.
rows.factual_conclusion: Only format major version 3 is accepted for game id 2. Any other major version stops the read and is counted as unsupported.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the engine accepts a 3.x minor version other than 9.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate refusal, reported as such.

rows.source_detail: Hand-built synthetic .pex fixtures with one malformed field each.
rows.factual_conclusion: A string index outside the table, a declared object size that is neither convention, a variable-argument count that is negative, non-integer or past the end of the file, and an unsupported major version each fail closed with a message.
rows.provenance_boundary: Synthetic fixtures only.

rows.source_detail: Four project-authored scripts compiled by a locally installed PapyrusCompiler.exe.
rows.factual_conclusion: Radicle reads the compiler's .pex and reproduces it byte for byte: 308, 447, 455 and 474 bytes, one object each, 0 to 3 instructions.
rows.provenance_boundary: Project-authored scripts and counts only; the tool stays outside the repository and its output goes to a temporary directory.

rows.source_detail: PapyrusAssembler.exe disassembles each compiled file and reassembles it.
rows.factual_conclusion: The factual instruction stream of the reassembled file matches the compiler's, and Radicle round-trips both, so its decode agrees with the encoding the assembler produces.
rows.provenance_boundary: Comparison of factual instruction fields only; no disassembly text is copied into the repository.

rows.source_detail: Mutagen's Papyrus Pex layer measured against the local corpus as a candidate backend.
rows.factual_conclusion: Mutagen's Pex layer failed to read about 65 percent of the local corpus and round-tripped 5 of 2,735 files byte-identically, so it is not a usable Papyrus backend.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts only. Mutagen remains a compatibility oracle for plugin records and is not a runtime path.

rows.source_detail: Five local .seq files of 4, 8 and 12 bytes; three project-authored probe variants, one deployed copy and one third-party mod file.
rows.factual_conclusion: A .seq is a bare array of little-endian uint32 runtime FormIDs: no header, no count, no magic and no trailing bytes. Every measured length is a multiple of four.
rows.provenance_boundary: Sizes, entry counts and the entry width only. No corpus file or name is committed.

rows.source_detail: The project's own SEQ writer and xEdit's Create SEQ File path, which writes each quest's runtime FormID.
rows.factual_conclusion: An entry carries the master index in bits 24-31 and the local FormID in bits 0-23, which is the runtime FormID layout Radicle already models as RawFormId.
rows.provenance_boundary: Field layout only; the reference tool is cited, not copied.

rows.source_detail: Synthetic fixtures with ascending, descending and duplicate entries.
rows.factual_conclusion: Entries are preserved exactly and in file order. A 0xFFFFFFFF, created-index or light-runtime-index entry is ordinary data and is not special-cased.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the engine requires entries to be sorted or unique.
rows.provenance_boundary: Synthetic fixtures only.

rows.source_detail: Garden's refusal, verified with synthetic fixtures of 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 255 bytes.
rows.factual_conclusion: A byte count that is not a whole number of four-byte entries is rejected with a parse error at the offending offset.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine does with such a file.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate refusal, reported as such.

rows.source_detail: No measured file is empty, and the project's writer refuses to write a SEQ with no entries.
rows.factual_conclusion: Radicle reads a zero-byte .seq as an empty list. Whether the engine accepts one is unknown.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Engine behavior for a zero-byte .seq.
rows.provenance_boundary: No empty file exists in the local corpus.

rows.source_detail: No runtime probe has been run; the writer's rule comes from xEdit's behavior, not from the engine.
rows.factual_conclusion: Precedence between several plugins' .seq files, and between a SEQ entry and the plugin's own record flags, is unknown.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Which plugin's SEQ entries the engine honors when more than one plugin provides them.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as an open gap rather than assumed.

rows.source_detail: The container carries no load order, so an entry cannot be resolved from the file alone.
rows.factual_conclusion: How the engine resolves an entry's master index at runtime, and whether it must equal the plugin's load-order slot, is unknown. Radicle never resolves an entry to a FormKey.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The runtime meaning of the master index byte in a SEQ entry.
rows.provenance_boundary: Reported as an open gap.

rows.source_detail: All 1,336 QUST records in Fallout4.esm decoded, plus synthetic fixtures.
rows.factual_conclusion: A quest's VMAD leading script list decodes into script names with typed properties. The sweep found 917 script attachments across the shipped quests.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts and decoded field shapes only.

rows.source_detail: All 1,336 QUST records decoded; 7,150 stage fragments found, plus synthetic fixtures.
rows.factual_conclusion: The quest VMAD block that follows the script list carries, per stage fragment, the stage, a stage index, the fragment script name and the fragment function name, and the fragment script's typed properties.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts and decoded field shapes only.

rows.source_detail: All 1,336 QUST records decoded; 2,235 alias script attachments found, plus synthetic fixtures.
rows.factual_conclusion: Each alias entry in the quest VMAD carries its alias id and that alias's script attachments with their typed properties.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts and decoded field shapes only.

rows.source_detail: The project's own SEQ writer reads the same bit; the decode was checked against all 1,336 shipped quests.
rows.factual_conclusion: A quest's start-game-enabled flag is bit 0 of the first uint16 of its 12-byte DNAM subrecord.
rows.provenance_boundary: Field layout only.

rows.source_detail: Garden's refusal to guess, verified with a truncated extras block and with the shipped-quest sweep.
rows.factual_conclusion: A missing quest, a non-QUST record, duplicated DNAM or VMAD, a DNAM that is not 12 bytes, an unsupported VMAD property type, extras that do not consume fully, or a failed VMAD decode each produce a named unsupported reason instead of a guess.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate refusal, reported as such.

rows.source_detail: No runtime probe has been run.
rows.factual_conclusion: The order in which the engine creates quest scripts and calls OnInit and OnQuestInit at startup is unknown.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Startup ordering and script creation timing.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as an open gap.

rows.source_detail: No runtime probe has been run.
rows.factual_conclusion: When a stage fragment runs relative to SetStage, and what happens to fragments whose stage never fires, is unknown.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Stage fragment dispatch timing.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as an open gap.

rows.source_detail: No runtime probe has been run.
rows.factual_conclusion: The order in which aliases fill, and how a fill interacts with the scripts attached to that alias, is unknown.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Alias fill order.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as an open gap.

rows.source_detail: Recorded in docs/proof/papyrus-interpreter-decision.md.
rows.factual_conclusion: Garden executes Papyrus bytecode in its own managed VM inside the existing GameSession and ScriptHost, fed by Radicle's decode. No Mutagen type is loaded at runtime and no decompiler output is translated.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate architectural decision, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: How default values initialize variables and properties, and what assignment does to an unset property, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Default initialization and assignment semantics.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: Whether arguments are passed by value, and how a missing or extra argument behaves, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Parameter passing semantics.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: What a function returns when no return statement runs, and how a return inside a state behaves, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Return and control flow semantics.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: The exact result of a cast between each pair of Papyrus types, and of an is test on a null or mismatched value, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Cast and type test results.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: Integer division and modulo behavior on negative and zero operands, and float comparison of NaN, are not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Arithmetic and comparison edge behavior.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: The behavior of an out-of-range array read or write, of array_findelement on a missing value, and of array_add on a fixed-size array, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Array edge behavior.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: How struct values are copied, compared and passed, and what a struct_get on a missing member does, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Struct semantics.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: Property get and set dispatch, and which parent function a callparent reaches, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Property and function dispatch.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: What GotoState does when the target state does not exist, and whether a running function continues in the old state, is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: State lookup and GotoState behavior.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: Probe planned; not run.
rows.factual_conclusion: When OnInit runs relative to property defaults and to the parent's OnInit is not yet proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: OnInit ordering.
rows.provenance_boundary: Unrun probe; no claim is made.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records that waits and latent behavior are not yet proven.
rows.factual_conclusion: A latent wait parks its event and is counted as an approximation. It is never reported as completed, and its resumption is not claimed.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How a latent wait parks a function, what resumes it, and what happens to it when its owning object unloads.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate partial behavior; the reliance is counted, not hidden.

rows.source_detail: The documented Data-folder load order: a loose file overrides an archive, and a later entry in the load order overrides an earlier one.
rows.factual_conclusion: The script cache resolves one winner per script name: loose beats archive, a higher load index beats a lower one, and an ordinal container-path comparison breaks any remaining tie, so the winner never depends on enumeration order.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How the engine breaks a tie between two loose copies of the same script in the same load-order slot.
rows.provenance_boundary: The rule Garden implements, reported as a policy rather than as a measured engine behavior.

rows.source_detail: A local corpus run: 8,533 official .pex entries dumped with Radicle's own BA2 reader and fed to the cache through an injected reader.
rows.factual_conclusion: The archive path runs end to end on real data: the game-side enumerator opened the five official archives with Radicle's own BA2 reader, selected 8,533 scripts with no duplicate names, and read every payload — all 8,533 start with the PEX magic, none is empty, and each length matches its entry — and the cache wrote 8,533 manifest entries with 0 absent and 0 fingerprint mismatches.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether Radicle enumerates every script entry a real load order would use, and in which order archives participate in it, stay unproven: this run covered the five official archives and not a load order.
rows.provenance_boundary: A local corpus measurement. Counts and the manifest only; no corpus file, name or content is published.

rows.source_detail: Records the tip of GARDEN-TOOLS nomad/dev after pull requests #845, #846 and #847 merged, at C ABI 59: the full Papyrus runtime (struct opcodes, GoToState, resumable slices and latent calls, the scheduler, instances and registrations, the save state and the quest rules).
rows.factual_conclusion: The Papyrus runtime pins GARDEN/GARDEN-TOOLS commit 2db5f1d3285b25cf06fe3d34a8a5dae4d671a2a5 at C ABI version 59, the tip of nomad/dev; every cache manifest records that pin so a mismatch is a recorded fact, and a test asserts RADICLE_COMMIT in opencw/native/radicle/CMakeLists.txt equals the constant.
rows.provenance_boundary: A build pin, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the compiled-cell attachment model.
rows.factual_conclusion: A compiled reference node carries its script attachments as fo4_scripts metadata in the properties JSON shape, with fo4_script_duplicate_names and fo4_script_unsupported_values counts when they are non-zero. An unsupported value carries a reason and a null value instead of a PEX default, and floats are always invariant.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the engine applies a reference's script property values before or after the base object's defaults at runtime.
rows.provenance_boundary: The compiled-cell contract Garden defines, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Pinned Radicle 34d16d50 at ABI 9 exposes typed reference VMAD through PlacedReference; seven synthetic native-to-compiled-metadata cases pass.
rows.factual_conclusion: The compiled-cell producer consumes Radicle's typed reference properties, uses invariant numeric text, refuses alias-bound values and preserves the record-level partial-decode flag. Synthetic cases establish those conversion boundaries, not full real-data or engine compatibility.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether a Radicle reference VMAD surface reproduces every value the current producer emits, including object values that need a load order.
rows.provenance_boundary: Project-authored plugin fixtures and the pinned Radicle decoder; no Fallout runtime or alias-fill claim. The read-only NonVR reference was unavailable during this follow-up.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records the fail-closed model errors.
rows.factual_conclusion: A malformed program, an out-of-range local, a division by zero, a missing struct member or a native that cannot be resolved stops the VM with a model error instead of producing a value.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate Garden decision, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records the explicit frame stack and the no-C#-recursion rule.
rows.factual_conclusion: Garden executes Papyrus calls on an explicit frame stack with a bounded depth, never on the C# call stack, and reports a depth failure instead of overflowing.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate Garden design decision, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records one shared ScriptHost for quest and reference scripts.
rows.factual_conclusion: One ScriptHost owns the library, the attached instances, the native registrations and the ready queue; the runtime never constructs a second interpreter.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate Garden design decision, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records that what happens to an event arriving during OnInit is separately unproven.
rows.factual_conclusion: An event that arrives while OnInit is running is refused by default, and may only be queued when the caller accepts the approximation, in which case every queue is counted.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine does with an event that arrives while OnInit is running.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate partial behavior; the reliance is counted, not hidden.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records the proven ordering barrier and the failed-OnInit rule.
rows.factual_conclusion: OnInit runs once, after properties are attached, and no later event may run before it completes. A failed OnInit leaves the script failed closed and later events are refused.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: When OnInit runs relative to property defaults and to the parent's OnInit.
rows.provenance_boundary: The barrier Garden enforces, not a claim about the ordering the engine uses.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records the Static, ScriptInstance and EngineObject target contract.
rows.factual_conclusion: A native call resolves through an explicit target: a static call needs a global function, a script-instance call needs the attached ScriptObject of the required script, and an engine-object call needs an engine identity. The VM never guesses an attached script from a bare reference.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate Garden contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The Papyrus Runtime VM page records deterministic instruction budgets instead of Fallout's time-budget implementation.
rows.factual_conclusion: The host delegates queued events to the bounded scheduler. Each slice preserves event-owned frames, PCs, locals and return slots. Completed events are removed, so budget accounting cannot repeat their side effects.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How the engine budgets script time.
rows.provenance_boundary: Garden engine behavior, explicitly not claimed as vanilla parity.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the census against the runtime's own resolution rules.
rows.factual_conclusion: The census resolves script and function names with the same ScriptLibrary rules the runtime uses, counts each native target by static and method kind, and reports loaded, unreadable, not-loadable and ambiguous scripts as separate categories plus the unresolved call sites. The report is ordinally sorted, so the same input is byte-identical in any order.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden measurement contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: A local corpus run: 9,517 payloads decoded with Radicle's own BA2 and PEX readers and fed to the census through the library's own resolution rules.
rows.factual_conclusion: The static census ran over 9,032 scripts: 15,500 statically resolvable call sites, all resolved (0 unresolved, 0 unreadable, 0 not-loadable, 0 ambiguous), naming 111 native targets. That run attributed no callmethod site; the operand roles that make one attributable are measured separately.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The 111 targets are lowercased script names and nothing checked whether a callee is native. The 109,023 callmethod instruction count came from the probe's own counter and needs the private corpus, so it is not re-derivable here.
rows.provenance_boundary: A local corpus measurement. Counts and the target list only; no corpus file or script body is published.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the base native set.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every bound native declares the evidence key that gates it, and a registration without one is rejected. The base set is Garden's own Debug sinks; a name the set does not bind is refused and counted.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden contract, not a claim about the engine's natives.

rows.source_detail: Bound to a Garden sink, not to the engine's UI.
rows.factual_conclusion: A Debug.MessageBox call is accepted and reported to the host sink. Nothing about the engine's own message box behavior is claimed.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine's own Debug.MessageBox does.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden sink, not engine parity.

rows.source_detail: Bound to a Garden sink, not to the engine's UI.
rows.factual_conclusion: A Debug.Notification call is accepted and reported to the host sink. Nothing about the engine's own notification behavior is claimed.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine's own Debug.Notification does.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden sink, not engine parity.

rows.source_detail: Bound to a Garden sink, not to the engine's log.
rows.factual_conclusion: A Debug.Trace call is accepted and reported to the host sink. Nothing about the engine's own logging behavior is claimed.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine's own Debug.Trace does.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden sink, not engine parity.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the bounded scheduler.
rows.factual_conclusion: A step runs ready events in arrival order within their share of the instruction budget. Exhausted events retain their execution state for the next step. A bounded slice counter belongs to each queued event; reaching its limit drops and counts that event.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How the engine budgets script time.
rows.provenance_boundary: Garden engine behavior, explicitly not claimed as vanilla parity.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing reflection registration.
rows.factual_conclusion: A method marked with the override attribute is registered from reflection, and a marked method whose signature is not an override is rejected instead of skipped.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the synchronous override registry.
rows.factual_conclusion: An override is asked for only at a bytecode entry point, so it never intercepts a native call and never receives a bare reference. A handled override replaces the bytecode and its value is the result, a declined override falls through, and a function the script does not define or a wrong argument count is refused before the handler runs.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the engine offers any equivalent interception point.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden feature, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the cell session.
rows.factual_conclusion: Activation is routed through the session to the instance the reference is bound to. An activation for a parked reference or an unknown reference is refused and counted, with a different reason for each case.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden routing contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing detach and reattach.
rows.factual_conclusion: Detaching a cell parks its reference instances instead of destroying them, and reattaching restores the same instances, so a script keeps its identity and lifecycle across a stream.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden lifecycle contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The split landed in commits 7d52955f and 2e513ccc: the cell streaming lifecycle moved verbatim into WorldspaceStreamer.Lifecycle.cs, methods only, beside the seven partial files that already existed.
rows.factual_conclusion: The WorldspaceStreamer lifecycle now has its own partial file. Only methods moved: no field, property, nested type or initializer changed file, the base list stays on the original declaration, and the member set is unchanged at 106 declarations, so the split is behaviour-neutral by construction and the project compile check passes on it.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The running game was not exercised: behaviour-neutrality rests on the move being methods-only with an unchanged member set, not on an observed session.
rows.provenance_boundary: A structural measurement of this repository: file and member counts plus the CI compile check. No engine runtime was run.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the session tick.
rows.factual_conclusion: The session tick hands the budget to the host and does nothing else, so no scheduling logic lives in the session.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the startup converter.
rows.factual_conclusion: The converter never parses SEQ bytes: Radicle decodes the container and hands over raw FormIDs. An unproven container produces no startup data, an empty file is skipped and reported, a not-read file is reported separately, and the output is written under a rename swap that leaves either the old or the new file.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden conversion contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The converter keeps the raw FormID and reports the approximation.
rows.factual_conclusion: A startup entry carries the raw FormID exactly as the file did. The master index is never resolved, and the report says so.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How the engine resolves an entry's master index at runtime.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate partial behavior; the reliance is reported.

rows.source_detail: The converter keeps entries per plugin and reports the approximation.
rows.factual_conclusion: When more than one plugin contributes entries they are kept per plugin in file order and never merged, because precedence between plugins is unproven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Which plugin's SEQ entries the engine honors when more than one plugin provides them.
rows.provenance_boundary: A deliberate partial behavior; the reliance is reported.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the quest startup preflight.
rows.factual_conclusion: Startup preflights every start-game-enabled quest before anything is touched: a quest whose startup ordering, stage-fragment timing or alias fill order is unproven is blocked, and a not-start-enabled quest is skipped.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden startup contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the transactional apply.
rows.factual_conclusion: A plan is applied only when nothing is blocked, so an unsupported behavior blocks the run before mutation: no instance is attached and the blocked and approximation counters each advance exactly once per blocked quest. Quest-owned scripts attach through the host the caller passes, and the plan report is ordinally ordered.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden startup contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the acceptance runner.
rows.factual_conclusion: The acceptance run resolves each effective script's parent chain to an engine-type seed and reports a missing parent, a cycle, a depth overrun and an unknown startup plugin as separate failures. The report is ordinally sorted, carries a SHA-256 digest, and the summary counts equal the listed failures.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden reporting contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The profile load order ran through Mo2ProfileLoader, RadicleQuestStartup, GameLoader.ArchiveOrder, RadicleArchiveScripts, LooseScriptSource and Radicle.Interop.PexFile, fed to LoadOrderAcceptance unchanged.
rows.factual_conclusion: The real-load-order acceptance ran through the shipped readers over the Fallen World profile: 657 plugins, the 444 archives they load plus loose scripts by MO2 priority, 14,643 scripts with every chain resolved, 1,016 real startup quests, 0 unknown plugins, digest 26ac42cb. 9 attachments name 2 scripts that no file in the install provides.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Precedence between two archives carrying the same script is the shipped ArchiveOrder, not measured against the game; startup execution order and timing are unproven.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts and a digest only; the corpus, its file names and its script contents stay local.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the coverage baseline.
rows.factual_conclusion: The baseline gives owner types, attached scripts, native call sites, event handlers and fragments a counted row with a stable id, and gives every unsupported or unverified evidence key and every missing Garden system its own row. The report is ordinally sorted with a digest, and a closure that names a row the baseline does not have is refused.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden reporting contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The real full-load-order baseline has not been built: its inputs need Radicle's decode through the managed binding and the private local corpus.
rows.factual_conclusion: No real coverage baseline exists yet. The row model, the statuses, the reproducibility and the closure mechanism are pinned by the synthetic suite, and the real run will use them unchanged.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the real full-load-order counts are for each group, and which rows a later Part C task actually closes.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as not executed rather than implied by the synthetic suite.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the owner identity.
rows.factual_conclusion: A Papyrus owner carries its kind, its base form key and a discriminator, and equality is over all three, so two placed references, two aliases of one quest or two runtime instances of one base form stay distinct even though they share a base FormKey. Key is the stable text form an identity map, a thread table or a save record keys on, and an owner without a base form key is refused.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden identity contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: No probe has been run to compare Garden's owner identity with the engine's.
rows.factual_conclusion: Garden's owner identity is a deliberate model. Whether the engine distinguishes the same owners the same way, and what it uses as the identity of a dynamic reference or an alias, is not proven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine treats as the identity of a dynamic reference, a quest alias and a runtime instance, and whether two owners of one base form stay distinct in its save data.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than assumed from Garden's model.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the event bridge.
rows.factual_conclusion: PapyrusEventBridge is the only route from a Garden system to owner-local Papyrus events. Delivery is gated on the event's own evidence key; a targeted event reaches only its owner and a broadcast reaches every registered owner that declares the handler; a parked owner is skipped; arguments pass through verbatim; and every outcome is counted.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden routing contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: No probe has compared Garden's delivery with the engine's.
rows.factual_conclusion: Which events the engine produces, in what order, and to which instances they are delivered, is not proven. Garden delivers only events whose own key allows it and refuses the rest.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's event set, ordering and delivery targets for each family of engine-produced events.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than assumed from Garden's model.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the registration registry.
rows.factual_conclusion: Each registration keeps its full payload, dispatch matches on that payload, and only the session advances the runtime: an advance from any other owner is refused and counted. Real-time timers fire on accumulated time and a one-shot removes itself; game-time timers stay unbound and are counted.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden registration contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: No game-time clock source and no probe exist, so game-time timers are deliberately unbound.
rows.factual_conclusion: Garden has no game-time clock, so a game-time timer never fires and every attempt to advance one is counted. Real-time timers use a clock Garden owns.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What the engine's game-time clock is, whether it advances while paused, and how it relates to a script timer's interval.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unbound rather than approximated with the wrong clock.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the VM-only gap register.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every VM-only key is reported as closed (implemented and allowed by the gate) or open (refused and counted), and a key with no registry row fails closed. The register changes no status; it reports what the recorded registry and the gate already say.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden reporting contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the promotion rule.
rows.factual_conclusion: A key may only be PROVEN when its registry row records that a probe actually ran; the register lists any PROVEN row whose probe status is not run, so a result cannot be promoted without its logged evidence. The recorded registry currently promotes nothing without evidence.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden evidence rule, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Bound to pure operations on the arguments, which Garden owns.
rows.factual_conclusion: Math.Abs, Floor, Ceiling, Min and Max operate only on their arguments, so Garden binds them and refuses a non-numeric argument instead of guessing a coercion.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the engine's Math natives coerce their arguments the same way.
rows.provenance_boundary: Garden arithmetic on the arguments, not engine parity.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the family binding.
rows.factual_conclusion: A native family is bound whole or refused whole, never half-bound: an unsupported category stops and is counted with its reason instead of being reported as generically supported. The report is ordinally ordered with a digest.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden binding contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Nine families are refused because they need a gameplay system Garden does not have yet.
rows.factual_conclusion: Utility, GameQuery, Form, ObjectReference, GlobalVariable, FormList, Keyword, Cell and PlaceAtMe bind nothing. Their behavior and the gameplay systems they read are unproven, so each is refused and counted as a family.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What each of those families does, what engine data it reads, and which Garden system will own it.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as refused rather than reported as generically supported.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the VMAD value binder.
rows.factual_conclusion: Properties stay owner-local. Scalars bind; non-alias objects carry their decoded identity in EngineObjectReference, never a string or attached script. Alias objects, undecoded arrays/structs, variables and unknown kinds remain explicit unsupported shapes with reasons. Unsupported values never receive PEX defaults.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden binding contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Radicle stops at the element count for an array or struct, so the elements are not decoded.
rows.factual_conclusion: An array or struct property is bound to nothing and reported with its element count, so a partially decoded shape is never presented as a complete value.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How the elements of a VMAD array or struct are encoded and how Garden should reproduce them.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unsupported rather than approximated with a partial value.

rows.source_detail: The alias fill order is unproven, so an alias-bound object is not resolved.
rows.factual_conclusion: An object property that is bound to a quest alias binds to nothing and is reported, because resolving it needs the alias fill system.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: When quest aliases are filled and which object an alias-bound property should receive.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unsupported rather than resolved by guess.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the lifecycle driver.
rows.factual_conclusion: Reference lifecycle transitions are delivered only through the event bridge, so they share its gate, targets and counters. The driver holds no host reference, and a parked owner receives nothing until it is unparked.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden routing contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The behavior of an unloaded reference has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: While the unloaded-reference behavior is unproven the owner is parked and the uncertainty is counted, and the count disappears only when the evidence key actually allows the event. The temporary parking policy is therefore replaced by proof rather than by assumption.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether the engine delivers an unload event to a reference script, when, and whether the instance survives.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as parked and counted rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the startup-stage identification.
rows.factual_conclusion: A staged quest starts at the single stage Radicle marked as the startup stage. A quest with no marked stage, or with more than one, is left unresolved and counted: the first stage is never assumed and a tie is never broken by index. An identified stage whose fragment dispatch timing is unproven keeps the quest blocked, and an unproven identification key chooses nothing.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden startup contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The decoder supplies the startup-stage marking; the engine's own stage flags have not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: Whether the engine's startup-stage marking is what Garden reads, and how it treats a quest with none or several, is not proven. Garden reads only what the decoder reports and guesses nothing.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's startup-stage flag semantics and its behavior for a quest with no marked stage or several.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than inferred from Garden's contract.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the stage dispatcher.
rows.factual_conclusion: While the fragment dispatch timing is unproven the whole stage is refused and counted, so B9's refusal stands. When it is proven the quest-owned fragments of the changed stage run on the quest's own script instance in fragment order, and the stage applies only if every one of them exists; a missing function refuses the stage whole rather than half-applying it.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden dispatch contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Alias-owned fragments are deferred to C12a; nothing runs them.
rows.factual_conclusion: A fragment owned by a quest alias is deferred and counted and never run, so this task does not claim alias remote-event acceptance. Only quest-owned fragments run.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Which alias receives a stage fragment, and when the engine dispatches it to that alias.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as deferred rather than claimed as working.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the quest state model.
rows.factual_conclusion: Start, Stop, Reset and CompleteQuest move the quest between NotStarted, Running, Stopped and Completed. An illegal transition is refused and counted rather than forced, and every targeted native is bound or blocked by a named key in the report.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden state contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Whether SetActive changes the running state has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: SetActive is blocked and never transitions a quest, so a state change never relies on an unproven rule.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Whether SetActive starts, stops or only flags a quest, and how it interacts with Start and Stop.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as blocked rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the condition evaluator.
rows.factual_conclusion: The six comparison operators are Garden arithmetic on the decoded values. OR-bearing conditions are explicitly unsupported until grouping is verified. An unsupported condition never defaults true or false: if any member of a list is undecided the whole list is indeterminate, every function is counted by its exact name, and an empty list decides nothing.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden evaluation contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: No CTDA condition function has been probed, so none is registered.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every condition function used by the load order is counted by its exact name and none is evaluated, because no function has a proven implementation. A function is registered only when its own key allows it.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: What each CTDA condition function reads and returns, one function at a time from evidence.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unsupported rather than defaulted.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the non-actor alias fills.
rows.factual_conclusion: Forced-reference, create-reference and location fills work without the actor runtime: a forced reference binds the declared reference, a created reference allocates a fresh dynamic owner so two creations of one base stay distinct, and a location records its form key. Each kind has its own evidence key, so an unproven kind leaves only its own alias empty and counted.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden fill contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Find-matching and unique-actor fills need the actor runtime, which C11b owns.
rows.factual_conclusion: Find-matching and unique-actor aliases are left empty and counted; they are never filled here, and the task does not claim actor alias fills.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How the engine selects a matching or unique actor for an alias and when the fill happens.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as open for C11b rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the alias runtime.
rows.factual_conclusion: Only a filled C11a alias gets an owner and a script: it runs its own script on the shared host, binds its properties through the VMAD binder so an unsupported shape stays explicit and owner-local, and the objective state lives in this runtime, which is therefore authoritative for it. An open alias is skipped and counted.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden alias contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the registered-recipient delivery.
rows.factual_conclusion: An alias receives Quest.OnStageSet only when it actually registered for that event through the C2b registry; an alias that did not register receives nothing and is counted, and delivery goes through the C2 event bridge.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden routing contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the actor owners.
rows.factual_conclusion: A placed actor is owned by its placed reference and a spawned actor by a dynamic reference, so two actors of one base form are always distinct owners and a placed and a spawned actor of one base never collide.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden identity contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Which of a base form's script and a reference's script wins, and in what order they run, has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: While the precedence is unproven nothing is merged: the actor is counted as unresolved and runs no script, rather than being run with a guessed order.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The inheritance and merge precedence between a base form's script and a reference's script, and their execution order.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unmerged rather than guessed.

rows.source_detail: Actor spawning, which the C4 PlaceAtMe category also leaves unsupported, has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: A spawned actor is not created while the spawn is unproven, so the categories C4 refused stay refused here and are counted.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How an actor is spawned, what its owner identity becomes, and what it inherits from its base form.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as refused rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the actor-dependent alias fills.
rows.factual_conclusion: A find-matching alias is filled only when its condition list is actually decided, so an indeterminate list leaves it unfilled and unbound and can never read as bound to None. A unique-actor alias is filled only when exactly one candidate matches; none or several is counted rather than guessed. Both kinds are gated on the actor fill key and stay counted while it is unproven.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden fill contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: How the engine selects a matching or unique actor for an alias has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: Which candidate the engine would pick, and how it treats several matches, is not proven; Garden fills only from a decided condition list or a single match and counts everything else.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's own matching and tie-breaking when several actors qualify for an alias.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than inferred from Garden's contract.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the actor alias binding.
rows.factual_conclusion: A filled actor-dependent alias records the actor it is bound to, gets its own script instance on the shared host and is registered with the event bridge, so its script runs against that actor. An alias C11b left unbound stays unbound and is named with its quest, alias and reason. Two aliases keep their own actors.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden binding contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: No probe has compared Garden's alias-to-actor binding with the engine's.
rows.factual_conclusion: Whether the engine binds an actor-dependent alias to the same actor, and when that binding happens, is not proven. Garden binds only what C11b actually filled and names everything else.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's own alias-to-actor binding and its timing.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than inferred from Garden's contract.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the actor event routes.
rows.factual_conclusion: A direct owner event goes straight to its owner through the C2 bridge. A registration-required event goes only to an owner that registered for it through the C2b registry, and a registration whose filter does not match is filtered out rather than delivered, so the register and filter behaviour is never bypassed. Both routes share the bridge and its counters.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden routing contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Which actor and combat events the engine publishes, and on which route, has not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: The engine's own actor event set, its filters and which of them require a registration are not proven. Garden routes only the families it is told about and refuses a route whose key is unproven.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: The engine's actor and combat event set, their filters, and which require a registration.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unproven rather than inferred from Garden's routing.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the inventory runtime.
rows.factual_conclusion: A world item is owned by its placed reference and an inventory item by a dynamic owner carrying the actor and the stack, so two stacks of one item are distinct. Add, Remove and Equip each have their own key and the count and equipped flag live in the runtime, which is authoritative for them. Container storage is refused and counted, and an inventory event needs a matching registration.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden inventory contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Container storage semantics have not been probed.
rows.factual_conclusion: An operation against container storage changes nothing and is counted, so unsupported storage semantics stay explicit rather than being treated like a carried stack.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How items are stored in and taken out of a container, and what the container's own inventory means for a script.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as unsupported rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the magic runtime.
rows.factual_conclusion: Every applied effect gets its own owner built from the effect, the target and an instance number, so two applications of one effect on one target are distinct. Apply, Dispel and AddPerk each have their own key, and an unproven key changes nothing and is counted.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden ownership contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the perk fragment path.
rows.factual_conclusion: A perk fragment runs on the shared host once its key allows it. A package fragment is blocked because the AI system does not exist, and the missing magic and AI package systems are named in the blockers list rather than silently skipped.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden fragment contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Garden has no magic system, so effects are owned but not simulated.
rows.factual_conclusion: The magic system is a named blocker: effects get owners and perk fragments run, but nothing simulates an effect's own behaviour.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How an active magic effect behaves, what it applies to its target and when it ends.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as a named blocker rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Garden has no AI package system, so package fragments cannot run.
rows.factual_conclusion: The AI package system is a named blocker: a package fragment is blocked and counted, and no AI behaviour is claimed.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: How an AI package runs, what its fragments do and when they fire.
rows.provenance_boundary: Recorded as a named blocker rather than approximated.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the pin gate.
rows.factual_conclusion: The gate reports a pin as Landed only when its commit is reachable from GARDEN-TOOLS main and its C ABI matches, and as NomadDev (accepted, not Landed) when it is reachable from the nomad/dev integration branch with the matching ABI. A feature-branch-only commit, a missing commit and an ABI mismatch are each refused with their own reason, and every probe is reported in a stable order.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden gate contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: The recorded pin 2db5f1d3285b25cf06fe3d34a8a5dae4d671a2a5 is the tip of GARDEN-TOOLS nomad/dev after pull requests #845, #846 and #847 merged; Git ancestry verifies that it is reachable from nomad/dev.
rows.factual_conclusion: The pin is reachable from GARDEN-TOOLS nomad/dev, so the pin gate returns NomadDev (accepted, not Landed) and Part B no longer depends on an unmerged feature branch. The pin is intentionally on the integration branch; GARDEN-TOOLS main stays at ABI 40 and GT #848 (nomad/dev into main) is open and unmerged.
rows.provenance_boundary: A structural measurement of the GARDEN-TOOLS repository, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the load-order acceptance runner, and exercised with real startup data from RadicleQuestStartup (1,016 quests, 0 unknown plugins).
rows.factual_conclusion: A plugin owns its records and its SEQ file; a script is owned by no plugin and is a global asset the effective set resolves by name, loose beating archive. A startup entry is checked against the load order for its plugin and against the effective set for the scripts its quest attaches, never plugin name against script name.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden acceptance contract, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Operand roles read from 1,502 loose payloads of a local install; 26,625 callmethod, 8 callparent and 8,465 callstatic instructions, every one decoded by Radicle's own reader.
rows.factual_conclusion: Over 1,502 loose payloads and 26,625 callmethod instructions, operand 0 is the called function's name (21,653 match a function declared in the corpus; the rest are engine natives) and operand 1 is the receiver, whose declared type resolves for 18,723; operand 2 is the result slot. callstatic is script, function, result and callparent is function, result.
rows.provenance_boundary: Operand roles and counts only. No corpus file, name or content is published.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the census's method-target rule.
rows.factual_conclusion: A method site is attributed to the receiver's declared type when the payload carries one, and reported unresolved and counted when it does not. The called function's name is carried alongside the target rather than used as it, because the census names owning scripts while the runtime dispatches on the name.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden naming policy, not a claim about the engine.

rows.source_detail: Recorded by building and testing the event contract against the recorded registry.
rows.factual_conclusion: Garden's emittable set is explicit and empty today: the library constructs six names, delivery needs an event row for the name, none exists, and no engine system constructs an engine event, so coverage counts every handler. A handler matches by its compiled name: case-insensitively, and a remote event by its ::remote_<Type>_<Event> function.
rows.provenance_boundary: A Garden contract over the recorded registry, not a claim about the engine's event set.

rows.source_detail: PexOperandCensusTests over the seven official script archives through Radicle ABI 9 (10,271 scripts).
rows.factual_conclusion: Operand roles: callmethod (name, receiver, result, args), callstatic (script, name, result, args), callparent (name, result, args), propget (name, receiver, result), propset (name, receiver, value), struct_get/set name at 2/1, is type at 2. Jump offsets are relative: 1,483 of 54,392 are negative and all land inside their function.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts only; no corpus file, name or content is committed or published.

rows.source_detail: RadiclePexLoweringTests.EveryOfficialScriptLowersRoundTripsAndRuns.
rows.factual_conclusion: strcat, the array add, insert, remove, clear and find operations, identifiers that name no parameter, local or own variable (inherited ::X_var, ::State), and jumps outside a function lower to an explicit Unsupported operation that stops the VM: 1,717 of 267,349 official instructions.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Their engine semantics are not measured, so they are not implemented.
rows.provenance_boundary: Counts only; no corpus file, name or content is committed or published.

rows.source_detail: The IR names a script instance variable operand; the VM has no storage model for it.
rows.factual_conclusion: An operation that reads or writes a script instance variable stops at this key instead of guessing storage, defaults or inheritance.
rows.unresolved_uncertainty: Instance variable storage, defaults and save behavior are not measured.

rows.source_detail: ScriptCacheBuilder and its tests.
rows.factual_conclusion: The machine-local cache stores lowered Garden IR as JSON .gir files and each winner's PEX payload (scripts/<name>.pex) beside it, each with its own SHA-256 (manifest format 5). Reuse needs the source SHA-256, both fingerprints, the IR format, lowering version and Radicle pin to match; other winners are reconverted, removed winners disappear and an interrupted swap recovers.

rows.source_detail: NativeSet, ScriptHost and their tests.
rows.factual_conclusion: A native is identified by its owning script and its function, compared without case, so two scripts can expose the same function name without colliding. A method native is looked up on the receiver type, then its parents.
